correctness.rationale: For q=2,3 PGL2 has (q+1)! elements and acts faithfully, hence all line-weight matchings occur. A two-ratio uncrossing argument shows a sorted assignment simultaneously no worse in max/min. Ordered ratio inequalities prove the n bound and both exact equality criteria. Explicit kernel-column generators realize both sharp families. For q=4, PGL2(F4)=A5; a transposition of distinct weights is infeasible, and integer ratio bounds certify the minimum 100/81. The embedded exact-arithmetic checker enumerated the declared finite cases and returned VERIFY_OK; the unbounded proof is algebraic.

value.rationale: Rank two is the first nontrivial dimension of the newly formalized Code Distortion Problem. The result replaces a general coarse distortion existence guarantee by an exact linear-time optimum for every length over two small fields, proves a sharp length bound and equality conditions, and demonstrates a concrete field-size transition at q=4. It solves a natural general subcase rather than reprinting a known numeric table.
